# Claude Meter

> Claude Meter is a free macOS utility that turns the MacBook camera notch into a Dynamic-Island-style panel showing your Claude subscription usage limits: the 5-hour session window, the weekly limit (all models), and any per-model weekly limits the account reports (for example Opus).

- Website: https://claudemeter.vercel.app/
- Download: https://claudemeter.vercel.app/ClaudeMeter.dmg (the site asks for an email for update notices, then the download starts)
- Source code: https://github.com/yiftach41/claude-meter (open source, MIT licence)
- Version: 1.2 (build 3) · Price: free · © 2026 Yiftach Freeman
- Signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
- Windows: not available yet. The website has a waitlist (name and email); one email when it ships.
- Independent project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Claude is a trademark of Anthropic, PBC.

## Requirements

- macOS 14.4 or later, Apple Silicon or Intel.
- Claude Code installed and signed in with a Claude Pro or Max subscription.
- Not supported: Claude Code signed in with an API key (Console), or a custom CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

## How it looks

- Collapsed: two readings either side of the notch. Session on the left (teal); on the right the weekly limit (lavender), or the tightest per-model limit (amber) when that one is higher. Percentages by default, or small tick bars.
- Peek (hover about 0.2 s): three rings (Session, Weekly, top model) with reset countdowns such as "resets in 2h 13m" and a session forecast line.
- Pinned (click): a table with a 6-hour sparkline, a bar (the session bar marks where it will land by reset), percentage and reset time, plus the plan name (e.g. "Max 20x") and when it last refreshed.
- Values above 85% turn red and bold. When a limit hits 100% a red note says e.g. "Opus limit reached · resets Sat 1:05 PM".
- Burn-rate forecast (session only): "hits the cap in 1h 12m" (amber; red if under an hour) or "on track — resets first".
- Macs without a notch, or a MacBook running lid-closed on an external display: a compact pill at the top centre. With the lid open the island stays on the built-in screen. Hides itself in fullscreen apps. No Dock icon.
- Optional menu-bar item: session and weekly (all models), as percentages or 1–5 blocks, red and bold above 85%. Clicking it opens the same menu as right-clicking the island.
- Appearance: Solid (pure black, fused to the notch), Frosted (heavy blur under a dark scrim), Liquid Glass (a thin glass sheet on macOS 26 with a rim lit from the pointer).
- Motion: panes squeeze in and out, digits roll, rings and bars draw from zero on open, and the island shrinks into the camera housing on launch, in full-screen apps and on Quit.
- First launch opens pinned with the hint "Hover to peek · click to pin · right-click for settings & Quit".

## Settings (right-click menu)

Live usage rows, Refresh now, Open usage on claude.ai, Appearance (Solid / Frosted / Liquid Glass), Show percentages, Burn-rate estimates, Usage notifications, Menu bar item, Launch at login, About, Quit.

## Notifications (opt-in)

Session at 50, 80 and 95%; weekly and per-model limits at 80 and 95%; and a "back to full" note when a window that had got tight resets.

## Updates

Refreshes every 5 minutes and when you hover, never faster than every 3 minutes because the usage endpoint rate-limits hard.

## Privacy and data

- Reads the sign-in Claude Code already saved on the Mac: the macOS Keychain item "Claude Code-credentials" via Apple's built-in `security` tool, falling back to ~/.claude/.credentials.json.
- Read-only: it never writes or changes those credentials. Short-lived access tokens are refreshed in memory only.
- Network: api.anthropic.com (usage), platform.claude.com (token refresh), and once a day https://claudemeter.vercel.app/version.json to check for updates.
- No analytics, no account, no server of its own.

## This website and your data

- The Mac download asks for an email; the Windows waitlist asks for a name and email. They are stored in the developer's Google Sheet, used only for Claude Meter updates and the Windows launch, and never shared or sold.
- No other tracking: no analytics or cookies. The page reads the public star count from api.github.com.

## FAQ

- Do I need Claude Code? Yes. It reads the sign-in Claude Code saves on your Mac.
- Will macOS ask about "security"? Usually not. If macOS asks to let "security" access "Claude Code-credentials", choose Always Allow; that is Apple's own keychain tool reading Claude Code's saved sign-in.
- How do I quit or uninstall? Right-click the island and choose Quit. To uninstall, drag the app from Applications to the Trash.
- Is it made by Anthropic? No.
- Is it open source? Yes, MIT: https://github.com/yiftach41/claude-meter
- Is there a Windows version? Not yet. Join the waitlist on the website.
